thread:
incident-bot: Pager — SEV: P1. inference-pool-usw2 showing repeated kubelet restarts -> nodes flipping NotReady (approx 5/12 nodes). Elevated 5xx and queueing on hosted API. Auto-scalers attempted to add capacity but new nodes also hit kubelet crashloops. Creating incident record: INC-2024-1719.
ryan: I'm on it — looking at node events and pod statuses now.
emily: tagging in. getting customer-impact numbers from metrics.
ryan: quick snapshot: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady` shows nodes n-gpu-12..16 NotReady. `kubectl describe node n-gpu-12` shows repeated kubelet restarts and the kernel logs have messages about `kworker` and GPU driver timeouts.
ryan: logs from pod inference-runtime-abc: `container killed with reason OOMKilled` on some pods, other pods show `ExitCode: 139` (segfault) and `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in runtime logs.
emily: metrics: hosted-api 5xx rate increased from 0.3% -> 6% over last 10m. p95 latency for generate endpoints increased ~220ms. A few high-volume customers are seeing throttles/timeouts in their jobs.
raj: are we seeing a common kernel/driver version on the failing nodes? maybe a bad driver rollout.
ryan: checking node labels: affected nodes are all on image `ami-infer-2024-11-02` with nvidia-driver 535.12. Non-affected ones are on 535.8.
infra-bot: Deploy history: `kube-daemonset/nvidia-drivers` updated 2024-04-10 03:02 UTC to 535.12 (deployed by infra-cd).
ryan: that matches. rolling driver update likely caused memory/driver instability under heavy load.
emily: customer-impact TL;DR — 7% of requests see errors, concentrated on long-seq generation workloads. Several customers opened support tickets. Impacting Embeddings generation jobs for analytics customers (batch jobs timing out).
samir: mitigation proposal: 1) cordon the failing nodes, 2) drain and evac pods to stable nodes, 3) fallback route for heavy customers to quantized / smaller model (reduce memory pressure), 4) scale up Dedicated pool in another AZ to absorb traffic.
ryan: executing step 1/2 now.
ryan: `kubectl cordon n-gpu-12 n-gpu-13 n-gpu-14`
ryan: `kubectl drain n-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
ryan: drain is kicking, but a few pods stuck in terminating due to PV mount locks.
emily: asking storage to help detach PVs for those pods. pinging @storage-team. :eyes:
raj: while we drain, we should trigger routing rule to divert new high-cost requests off the pool. emily can you flip the canary?
emily: flipping routing: updating route table to divert 25% of traffic from inference-pool-usw2 -> inference-pool-usw2-fallback (quantized). Command: `redwoodctl routes update --pool inference-pool-usw2 --split 75,25 --targets default,quantized-v2`
emily: done. Monitoring errors.
incident-bot: Action acknowledged by ryan. Pager acknowledged at 1719100023 by ryan.
ryan: watch: CPU on fallback nodes jumped but within limits. Error rate for main pool dropped to 3% after the routing change.
sre-lead: good. need quick remediation path for driver regression. Two options: roll back driver DS to 535.8, or move affected nodes to an older AMI. Rolling DS is faster but risky if new nodes already have 535.12 baked into AMI.
raj: I'd prefer roll back DS to 535.8 immediately for stability; plan a canary node first.
infra-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: `kubectl apply -f daemonset-nvidia-535.8-canary.yaml` -> will patch one node.
ryan: canary node reported healthy after driver 535.8. No kubelet restarts. Scaling up new nodes with 535.8 AMI started.
emily: Customer update drafted: "We are aware of elevated errors on generation endpoints and are diverting traffic to fallbacks while we remediate a GPU driver regression. We will update within 60 minutes." Approving to send.
samir: starting controlled rollback of DS to 535.8 in batches of 3 nodes.
ryan: rolling rollback in progress. patch applied to nodes in batches. Monitoring kubelet stability and pod restarts.
raj: adding temporary autoscaler rule: prefer fallback pool when instance health < 80% to prevent cascading backfill.
emily: monitoring dashboards — 5xx down to 1.2%, p95 latency returning toward baseline. Some jobs still queued; support notified customers with ETA 45m.
ana-next-oncall: (should be "ana-next-oncall") Sorry jumping in — I'm on deck for the next hour. what's the current status?
sre-lead: hey ana, handoff in 20. Summary: driver DS rollback to 535.8 underway, routing diverted 25% traffic to quantized fallback, draining affected nodes, storage helped detach PVs. Main pool error rate down to ~1%. Continue monitoring for 15m then confirm stable to close incident.
nana-next-oncall: got it. I'll monitor logs and paging. Anything you want me to keep an eye on specifically?
ryan: watch kubelet restart counts (`kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node`) and container OOM/139 exits in inference runtime pods. Also keep an eye on GPU driver dmesg lines for `NVRM: Xid` patterns.
emily: support update sent. Customer ack on two large accounts saying their batch jobs are re-running successfully.
sre-lead: if we see stability for 30m we'll move to postmortem. For now change status to `monitoring` and keep this channel active for any regressions.
raj: logging follow-up task — open a ticket to revert AMI build step that bumped driver, add a canary pipeline for driver ABI tests under load.
ryan: leaving primary oncall, handing to ana. I marked the runbook steps completed in the incident doc.
nana-next-oncall: acknowledged. Taking over now. Please @me for any escalations.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-1719 status -> monitoring. Last updated 1719103600.
sre-lead: thanks team. :clap: We should also schedule a short retro with infra-cd to prevent future driver rollouts without load-driven canaries.
nana-next-oncall: will create the follow-ups. monitoring windows open for 90m.
ryan: thanks all — good coordination.
